objections.claim: The spec's "single source of truth — the schema now enforces the bound" argument is only true when the bundled schema actually loads. The repo's evidence layer has a *designed* degrade path (evidence.js logRecordChecker/noteSchemaUnavailable, and commissaire.ts's own comment). Today conclusionRangeViolations is appended to the check result regardless of unavailable, so a three-item evidence_seq_range is still refused even when the bundle cannot be loaded. Deleting the function and its wiring makes the degrade path accept an over-long conclusion range on a path the spec never names.
objections.evidence: Spec rationale section on removing conclusionRangeViolations; commissaire.ts recordSchemaCheck.
objections.predicted_consequence: In any run where the evidence bundle is unavailable, a conclusion with >2 seq values is written where the current code refuses it.

objections.claim: Today the evidence_seq_range length bound is enforced unconditionally by conclusionRangeViolations. The spec deletes it and relocates the invariant entirely into the schema check, which has an explicit fail-open degrade when the bundle cannot be loaded. After this change, in degraded mode a conclusion record carrying a three-item evidence_seq_range is HMAC-signed and appended with no length check anywhere.
objections.evidence: Spec section 4 and the rationale to remove conclusionRangeViolations; commissaire.ts recordSchemaCheck/refuseOffSchema/noteUnavailable.
objections.predicted_consequence: During a schema-unavailable run, a conclusion with evidence_seq_range longer than two items is signed, chained, and persisted; audit replay reports it verified.

objections.claim: The spec requires that adding maxItems where none existed classifies as non-additive, yet no Given/When/Then scenario exercises that transition. A build could ship directional handling that catches raise/remove but lets the add case through, and every named scenario still passes.
objections.evidence: DONE item on maxItems added where absent; failure mode in section 4; scenario set covers raise, lower, and remove only.
objections.predicted_consequence: The add-where-absent case has no scenario, so a holdout or reviewer cannot decide that DONE item from the scenarios alone.
